origin: derived from a paired sim-stack audit: one sound sim (with controls and a stated prediction) run alongside two deliberately un-gated sims, so the divergence was observable

layer_meaning.generator: property of the code that produced the data (parameters, sampling rule, seed)
layer_meaning.physical: property of the modelled system, defensible outside this script
layer_meaning.instrument: property of the measuring apparatus (grid spacing, window, fit range, estimator)

guards.name: instrument resolution declared before run
guards.rule: for every measurement, state the instrument scale and the feature scale it must resolve; instrument scale must be finer by the stated margin
examples: k-grid spacing dk vs finite-sample peak width 2*pi/L
finite-size level spacing vs the splitting being swept
box-count smallest box vs mean nearest-neighbour distance
guards.fail_message: resolution not declared or instrument coarser than feature: output is not admissible
guards.rationale: an apparatus that cannot resolve the feature still emits numbers with plausible magnitudes

guards.name: controls sized by fragility, not by expected surprise
guards.rule: declare named controls with predicted values before running; a measurement expected to confirm requires controls first, not last
examples: feed a periodic lattice through the same S(k) code
feed a 1D line through the same dimension estimator
guards.fail_message: no controls declared: a confirming result cannot be distinguished from an artifact
guards.rationale: control budget tends to track anticipated doubt rather than measurement fragility, so the most fragile step gets the least scaffolding

guards.name: expected output written before execution
guards.rule: state in advance what the output should look like if the setup is working
examples: expect a dense point spectrum with many sharp peaks across the k-plane
guards.fail_message: no expected output recorded: divergence will not be visible
guards.rationale: an artifact is invisible against nothing and obvious against a written prediction

guards.name: every quantity tagged with its origin layer
guards.rule: each recorded number declares layer and the object it is a property of; no promotion between layers without an explicit step
examples: a branching-walk dimension is a generator property, not a property of the material being modelled
guards.rationale: generator-level and physical-level statements merge silently once they share a table

guards.name: ratios name both operands' objects
guards.rule: a ratio is admissible only if numerator and denominator are properties of the same object; otherwise it is void and carries no interpretation
examples: eigenvalue splitting over hopping integral, divided by an energy fraction in a branching rule, is void
guards.fail_message: ratio operands are properties of different objects: void, no interpretation permitted
guards.rationale: a labelled dimensionless number of plausible magnitude is accepted as physical

guards.name: every claim names the statistic supporting it
guards.rule: each claim lists recorded quantity names; a claim with no support is logged as unsupported and does not enter the conclusion
guards.rationale: demotion of a result to exploratory does not survive into a summary unless enforced

guards.name: statistic addresses the stated question
guards.rule: restate the question and name why the chosen statistic can discriminate it; a statistic blind to the property by construction must be flagged
examples: box-counting dimension is blind to quasiperiodic order by construction: uniform coverage returns the embedding dimension regardless of arrangement
guards.fail_message: no discrimination argument: statistic may be blind to the property under test
guards.rationale: the tested version drifts from the live version without a re-derivation step

guards.name: independence asserted, not assumed
guards.rule: before calling results convergent, state what is shared between them: same data, same generator, same predicted outcome
guards.fail_message: convergence asserted across measurements with shared inputs
guards.rationale: measurements on the same data whose outcome was predictable in advance are restatement, not corroboration
